summary: Replace full RunState recovery snapshots with compact Runtime Control Checkpoint v2 projections and durable truth references.
rationale: Recovery correctness requires coordinated runtime safe boundaries, SQLite-owned candidate and detail revisions, deterministic assembly, schema migration, and terminal compaction. The slice crosses runtime and runtime-control storage boundaries and cannot be split without reintroducing mixed checkpoint authority.
deletion_targets: full RunState copies in newly written recovery checkpoints
detail-open claim changes that force full RunState checkpoints
unbounded intermediate recovery checkpoints after terminal commit
line_count_rationale: The existing runtime orchestrator and Runtime Control SQLite store are oversized ownership boundaries. This vertical slice makes surgical changes in place; splitting those modules is a separate refactor outside the checkpoint scope.
risks: A checkpoint pointer could advance without the candidate truth revision unless every boundary remains in one SQLite transaction.
Compaction could remove resumable state before a terminal product outcome is durably committed.
Legacy v1 payload migration must fail closed without permitting new v1 writes.
